title: Record and communicate readiness
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Confirm site, authorised scope, safe access, serviceable kit and assigned tasks before beginning work.
Communicate a clear go/no-go decision with identified hazards, exclusions and support needed.
Record unresolved blockers and do not bypass access or safety controls.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Capture approved prestart evidence, report exceptions and obtain supervisor approval for scope or safety changes.

instruction.heading: Purpose and learning outcome
instruction.body: After this lesson, the learner can demonstrate record and communicate readiness in a routine cleaning workplace, identify limits of their authority and document the result. The following procedures are examples; always apply the approved site process and task instructions.

instruction.heading: Detailed workplace method
instruction.body: Before beginning, confirm correct site, authorised scope, safe access, serviceable kit, assigned tasks, communication channel and expected evidence. Use a concise readiness report stating go/no-go, identified hazards, exclusions and support needed. Notify the coordinator promptly if access fails, scope changes or a specialist hazard is found. Keep client details in approved records and avoid posting worksite images to personal chats.

instruction.heading: Safety, boundaries and escalation
instruction.body: Before proceeding, confirm the actual work scope, hazards, material or equipment suitability and who can authorise changes. Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside training, or the requested result conflicts with a site instruction. Record facts, not assumptions.

instruction.heading: Worked example
instruction.body: A cleaner cannot enter because the access code has expired. They log the failed attempt, contact the authorised coordinator and wait for verified instructions instead of asking a neighbour to open the premises.

instruction.heading: Supervised practical
instruction.body: Complete a mock pre-start briefing and readiness form for three scenarios: ready, delayed access and unsafe contamination.

instruction.heading: Assessment and corrective feedback
instruction.body: An assessor observes the learner and verifies: Communicates a clear go/no-go decision, records unresolved blockers and does not bypass access or safety controls. If any critical safety action is missed, provide coaching and require a new demonstration. Attendance alone is not proof of competence.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Before beginning, confirm the correct site, the authorised scope, safe access, serviceable kit, assigned tasks, the communication channel and the expected evidence.
Confirm the actual work scope, the hazards, the suitability of materials or equipment, and who can authorise changes.
Write a concise readiness report stating the go or no-go decision, the identified hazards, the exclusions and the support needed.
Record any unresolved blockers, and do not bypass access or safety controls.
Notify the coordinator promptly if access fails, the scope changes, or a specialist hazard is found.
If you cannot gain access, log the failed attempt and wait for verified instructions rather than asking a neighbour to open the premises.
Keep client details in approved records, and do not post worksite images to personal chats.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: The site, authorised scope, safe access, serviceable kit and assigned tasks are confirmed before work begins.
A go or no-go decision is communicated with the identified hazards, exclusions and support needed.
Unresolved blockers are recorded, and the coordinator is notified promptly if access fails.
Worksite images are not posted to personal chats, and client details are kept in approved records.
summary: Before work begins, the cleaner confirms the site, authorised scope, safe access, serviceable kit and assigned tasks.
A concise readiness report states a clear go or no-go decision, the identified hazards, the exclusions and the support needed.
Unresolved blockers are recorded, and access or safety controls are never bypassed.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which evidence or checks are essential when you record and communicate readiness?
options: Whether the weather looks nice for a photo and whether the client is pleased with the look of the job site
The correct site, authorised scope, safe access, serviceable kit and communication channel, before starting
How many people are in the group chat and whether the group chat is muted and who reads it
The client's preferred cleaning order and the order the rooms were cleaned last time by the team

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when access fails on arrival?
options: Start the job from the outside and sort access later and tell the client it is fine
Mark the job ready so the schedule holds and the crew starts on time anyway and the client is told
Ask a neighbour to open the premises so the job can start and the neighbour is then thanked
Log the failed attempt, notify the authorised coordinator promptly, and wait for verified instructions

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a readiness report state before work begins?
options: Go ahead because the job is booked and the client has paid the deposit already
Give a clear go/no-go decision, naming the hazards, exclusions and support needed
Decide go or no-go by which cleaner is most experienced on the day
Skip the report if the client has already been told and the crew knows the job well

knowledgeChecks.question: Which response to a failed site access is unsafe?
options: Sending the readiness form through approved channels
Reporting the failed access to the coordinator
Using a neighbour to get past an expired code
Stating the hazards and exclusions in the readiness report

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a readiness decision be recorded for the job file?
options: A concise readiness report recording unresolved blockers and the go/no-go decision
A verbal 'all good' with no record and the crew agrees on the day in the van
A photo of the client's keys in a personal chat and the address of the house
Nothing, if the job starts on time and the client is happy with the start
